correctness.rationale: For \(N\ge3\), \(-1\) is the unique order-two element in the cyclic subgroup \(\langle p\rangle\) once the supersingular congruence holds. Thus if \(d=\operatorname{ord}_N(p)\), the least admissible exponent is \(d/2\) and every other one is \(d/2+kd\). Harashita Lemma 7.7 gives the corresponding finite quotient of degree \(e_0^{2m+1}\), prime to \(p\), and Proposition 7.9 gives the \(p^{md/2}\) saturation and discriminant-group bounds plus prime-to-degree unimodularity. Monotonicity in \(k\) proves minimality within the cover family.

value.rationale: The p-adic descent theorem gives integral information only after choosing an admissible Hermitian parameter. Replacing that noncanonical choice by the least parameter \(q_0=p^{\operatorname{ord}_N(p)/2}\) produces a canonical computable saturation bound and simultaneously minimizes the finite cover used to generate cycles. This is a natural quantitative invariant for explicit middle-cycle computations on supersingular Fermat varieties, while the claim remains limited to the method bound rather than asserting an unsupported exact quotient exponent.
